item.title: Shiprocket IPO Subscribed 25.8X So Far On Final Day Of Bidding
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Ecommerce enablement platform Shiprocket’s ₹1,617.5 Cr IPO was subscribed 25.8X as of 13:06 IST on the final day of bidding,…
item.content:encoded:
Ecommerce enablement platform Shiprocket’s ₹1,617.5 Cr IPO was subscribed 25.8X as of 13:06 IST on the final day of bidding, as demand accelerated across investor categories. 

The issue received bids for 243.83 Cr shares against 9.44 Cr shares on offer, according to BSE data. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹885.5 Cr and an OFS component of about ₹732 Cr. 

NIIs led the demand, placing bids for 130.73 Cr shares against the 2.6 Cr shares reserved for them, translating into a subscription of 50.27X. 

Within the NII category, the portion reserved for applications above ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 55.65X, while the segment for bids between ₹2 Lakh and ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 39.49X. 

Retail investors bid for 50.26 Cr shares against the 1.73 Cr shares reserved for them, subscribing to their quota 28.99X.

Meanwhile, the employee quota was subscribed 34.46X.

Demand from QIBs also picked up sharply on the final day. The category received bids for 62.43 Cr shares against 5.1 Cr shares on offer, translating into a subscription of 12.25X. The QIB portion was subscribed just 3% at the end of the second day. 

Shiprocket’s IPO allotment is expected to be finalised on August 17 (Monday), while its shares are scheduled to list on the NSE and BSE on August 19 (Wednesday).

The IPO was subscribed 3.16X by the end of the second day of bidding, receiving bids for 29.8 Cr shares. Retail investors led the demand with a subscription of 9.7X, followed by NIIs at 4.8X. The employee quota was subscribed 13.3X.

Earlier this week, Shiprocket raised ₹727.4 Cr from anchor investors ahead of the IPO. The anchor book included domestic mutual funds such as HDFC Mutual Fund and global investors including Goldman Sachs, the New York State Teachers’ Retirement System, PGIM and Societe

item.title: Peak XV Leads $45 Mn Bet On US-Based AI Code Testing Startup Blacksmith
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Peak XV Partners led a $45 Mn Series B funding round of San Francisco-based AI code testing startup Blacksmith at…
item.content:encoded:
Peak XV Partners led a $45 Mn Series B funding round of San Francisco-based AI code testing startup Blacksmith at a valuation of $550 Mn, as the VC firm steps up investments in US-based AI and developer tools companies 

Existing investors Google Ventures (GV) and Y Combinator also participated in the round. Blacksmith closed the funding round in March 2026 but announced it now. The latest funding takes Blacksmith’s total capital raised to $58.5 Mn.

The startup plans to deploy a significant portion of the fresh capital to expand its computing infrastructure amid rising demand for tools that can test and validate AI-generated code. 

Blacksmith cofounder and CEO Aditya Jayaprakash said improvements in AI coding models are enabling developers to produce more software, creating a corresponding need for infrastructure to validate and test the code. 

“Every model improvement has expanded what coding agents can do and led to even more code being produced,” Jayaprakash said in a company blog post.

Founded in 2024 by Jayaprakash, Aditya Maru, and Aayush Shah, Blacksmith initially helped developers automatically test code before deployment. It is now building tools that allow developers and AI agents to validate and merge code faster. 

The startup said the number of continuous integration (CI) jobs run on its platform has grown 5%-10% week-on-week since the beginning of 2026, driven by the growing adoption of AI code generation tools. 

More than 6,000 companies now use Blacksmith, including Supabase, Clerk, Ashby and Mercury. 

Blacksmith is betting that existing CI infrastructure will struggle to handle the increase in pull requests and testing workloads as AI coding agents produce software at a faster pace.

The startup recently launched [code]smith, a cloud-based coding agent that can build features, fix bugs, diagnose CI failures, and automatically resolve them. It is also developing [code]smith QA, which will autonomously test code changes before they are merged. 

“The volume of code produced over the coming decade is only going to explode,” Jayaprakash said, adding that Blacksmith wants to help developers and AI agents validate and merge code faster. 

Blacksmith currently manages hundreds of thousands of CPU cores and plans to expand this footprint by around 10X over the coming months.

It competes with the likes of GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Buildkite, Depot, and Namespace. Blacksmith claims its purpose-built CI cloud infrastructure can run workloads up to twice as fast and at 50%-75% lower costs than GitHub-hosted runners.

Peak XV’s US Push

The investment comes as Peak XV expands its presence in the US and looks to tap AI and developer tools startups catering to the American market.

The VC firm began building its Bay Area presence after separating from Sequoia Capital in 2023. It subsequently hired operating partners in the US and brought former Y Combinator investor Arnav Sahu on board in 2025 to help lead its US investing efforts. 

Peak XV has since expanded its US team to eight members and opened its first San Francisco office. 

Its US portfolio includes San Francisco-based startups such as AI voice platform Vapi, AI memory infrastructure startup Mem0, AI sales training platform Hyperbound, and product development platform PostHog.

Peak XV has also backed Supabase, which offers an open-source alternative to Google’s Firebase, and AI infrastructure startup TrueFoundry.

item.title: ixigo To Sell 17.39% Fresh Bus Stake For ₹36.6 Cr
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Listed traveltech company ixigo has agreed to sell a 17.39% stake in electric intercity bus startup Fresh Bus to Twelve…
item.content:encoded:
Listed traveltech company ixigo has agreed to sell a 17.39% stake in electric intercity bus startup Fresh Bus to Twelve Stone LLP for ₹36.6 Cr. 

In an exchange filing, ixigo’s parent Le Travenues Technology said it will sell 46,264 CCPS of Fresh Bus at ₹7,911 apiece. 

Following the completion of the transaction, ixigo’s stake in Fresh Bus will decline from 25.66% to 8.27%. Consequently, Fresh Bus will cease to be an associate company of ixigo. 

The transaction is expected to be completed on or before August 30.

Twelve Stone’s designated partners are Fresh Bus founder and MD Sudhakar Reddy Chirra and Sasya Chirra. ixigo said the deal does not fall under the ambit of a related-party transaction. 

Founded in 2019 by second-time entrepreneur Sudhakar, Fresh Bus manages a full-stack EV bus platform. The startup claims that its electric buses have noise-free air-conditioned cabins, IOT-enabled real-time air-quality and temperature monitoring, security CCTVs, personal charging docks, Wi-Fi, real-time tracking and alcohol checks.

It competes against GreenCell Express, IntrCity SmartBus, ZingBus and gogoBus in the online bus aggregator and operator market.

ixigo first invested in Fresh Bus under an investment and shareholders’ agreement signed in October 2022. It acquired 68,258 CCPS and one equity share in the startup at ₹2,344 apiece. 

As of March 31, 2026, ixigo’s investment in Fresh Bus was valued at ₹18.87 Cr in its consolidated financial statements, accounting for 0.96% of its net worth. ixigo also recognised a ₹11.22 Cr share of loss from Fresh Bus in FY26. 

The stake sale comes amid ixigo’s acquisition spree. Earlier this year, the company announced its expansion into Europe through two different acquisitions in Spain-based train OTA platform Trenes (60% stake for €11.7 Mn) and AI company Sqaas ( 45.02% stake for €450K).

Later, ixigo’s board approved the acquisition of a majority stake in hotel booking startup Brevistay for ₹65.7 Cr. Besides, ixigo’s board also approved stake acquisitions in two AI startups – ProactAI  and Vestra.AI for about ₹12 Cr. 

Besides, reports claimed that ixigo was in advanced discussions to acquire the promoters’ stake in Yatra Online. However, Yatra later denied the reports.

On the financial front, ixigo’s consolidated PAT jumped 81% YoY to ₹34.2 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹18.9 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Operating revenue rose 13% YoY and 16% QoQ to ₹356.8 Cr. 

At 11:38 IST, shares of ixigo were trading 1.1% higher at ₹173.9 apiece on the BSE.
